evaluation_protocol.production: GroupShuffleSplit(0.2, rs=42) district-year groups; GroupKFold(5) CV on TRAIN only; metrics are on district TOTALS in tonnes (R2)
evaluation_protocol.f3_evaluation: same splitter family but different label set (renamed districts change sort order -> different groups selected); grouped OOF on train split + frozen holdout; metrics are within-+/-25% on t/ha
evaluation_protocol.different_holdout_rows_reason: district label spellings differ between the two tables, so the same seed selects different district-year groups

registry_metrics_not_comparable.note: different target scale, different rows, different loss — the production artifact has never been scored with the F3 within-+/-25% per-hectare protocol

registry_entry.algorithm: HistGradientBoostingRegressor on log(Yield_Tonnes / Area_Hectares) (Model M; exp(pred) * area)

production_vs_f3.verdict: NOT trained with the same code, data file, feature schema, target transform or evaluation rows as the evaluated F3 — the Phase 9-12 numbers describe an experimental per-crop model, not the served artifact

evaluation_splits.note: identical splitter parameters select different district-year groups because district label spellings differ between the enriched table (renamed) and the ICRISAT table (source names) — np.unique sorts by label, so the seeded permutation lands on different groups

phase_9_11_claim_check.assessment: Phase 9-11 never recorded an interpreter/library version. Their shared baseline constants (69.5352% OOF, 742/1088 holdout) reproduce ONLY on the evaluation stack (py3.14.6/sklearn 1.9.1), so all three phases ran there — internally one consistent environment. Their retain-F3 decisions are deltas measured within that single stack and are therefore internally valid. What does NOT transfer: the absolute metrics (the pinned serving stack scores 68.4679%/740 on the identical code) and any delta smaller than the measured 1.07 pp level gap. Phase 12 measured one candidate under both stacks (+0.267 vs +0.222 pp) suggesting deltas are stabler than levels, but n=1 — no Phase 9-11 claim can be certified under the serving stack without re-measurement, which this phase deliberately does NOT do (no new model experiments)
phase_9_11_claim_check.claims_rem_valid_single_env: YES for internal consistency (all three ran on one stack); NOT ESTABLISHED for the serving stack (untested there); absolute values are stack-specific

single_most_valuable_next_action.action: Collect district-resolution OBSERVED rainfall for 2000-2017 (minimum 2016-2017) and replace the Year.clip(upper=2015) forward-fill with real observations — before any further model work
single_most_valuable_next_action.why_first: only demonstrated data defect in the pipeline (10.04% of rows carry 2015 rainfall for later years), targets the three worst years (669 rows / 301 failures = 22.0% of all failures), needs no new dependency and no code change beyond the join, and the only already-available alternative (ERA5) was measured to HURT in Phase 9
single_most_valuable_next_action.strategic_second: field-/block-level yields address the largest cluster (bound 4.45 pp) but need institutional data sharing, not a download
